items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: Snoopy Young was great for doing that... he knew just exactly how to phrase your tunes.

ctx.x: Yes, I fooled around a little bit because I really wanted to get the sound, how it would but of it actually... I could picture it, you know, how it would sound with the brass and whatnot. And so I said, 'Well, I guess I'll try this, you know. So -- and sometimes, you know, when you make something like that -- I do anyway -- usually sketch out a routine, you know, what we call a little skate thing, first, you know. And you follow that pattern, and then sometimes I'll have a backup in case it doesn't turn out…

sound good because, you know, with seven brass and things like that, if you spread it out, it usually works out all right, especially if they punch, you know. Snoopy Young was great for doing that, and he had great conception. And seems like he knew just exactly how to phrase your tunes. You know, you didn't have to even put little markings in there. Of course, for certain guys like that, you know, little markings (unintelligible) that you use for phrasing. So it just kind of boosted your morale, as far as…

Right, when they just automatically know what to do with it. Did you find yourself -- we've talked a little bit about this before, but did you find yourself experimenting with different kinds of harmony changes? Did you look for different kinds of chord sounds or chord progressions?
